title: The Degrees Of Divine Unity And The Passage To The 2nd Stopping Place

questions.question: What did the traveler notice about believers and many Sufis?
questions.answer: They often say words that remind people Allah is One.

questions.question: What did that repeated saying show him?
questions.answer: It showed him that knowing Allah is One has many levels.

questions.question: How is saying and remembering Allah’s oneness described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is joyful, precious, high, and a kind of worship.

questions.question: What did the traveler want to do next?
questions.answer: He wanted to reach a higher level of understanding.

questions.question: What kind of knowing was he not looking for?
questions.answer: He was not looking for made-up or pretend knowing.

questions.question: What kind of knowing was he looking for?
questions.answer: He wanted sure knowledge based on proof.

questions.question: In this passage, what is true belief in Allah’s oneness like?
questions.answer: It means truly accepting that Allah is near and can be found with all things.

questions.question: When someone sees the world rightly, what do things become?
questions.answer: They become signs that lead to Allah.

questions.question: What should a person not think about the things in the world?
questions.answer: A person should not think they block him from Allah.

questions.question: What problem would happen if a person thought things were a barrier?
questions.answer: He would feel he had to push the whole world aside to find his Lord.

questions.question: What did the traveler do after speaking to himself?
questions.answer: He moved forward and came to a new place of learning.

questions.question: What did he see there across the whole universe?
questions.answer: He saw five big truths showing clearly that Allah is One.

questions.question: Why did the traveler pay attention to the way people of faith speak?
questions.answer: Because their words gave him a clue about Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: Which group is specially mentioned along with the people of faith?
questions.answer: People connected to a Sufi path.

questions.question: What were they doing again and again?
questions.answer: They were repeating words of tawhid and remembering Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about levels of tawhid?
questions.answer: A person can grow in it step by step.

questions.question: Besides being true, how is remembering Allah’s oneness described for the heart?
questions.answer: It is sweet and special for the heart.

questions.question: Is the traveler satisfied with a weak idea, or does he want strong proof?
questions.answer: He wants strong proof.

questions.question: What makes this knowledge strong?
questions.answer: It is built on evidence and certainty.

questions.question: How does a person with true tawhid look at the world?
questions.answer: He sees Allah’s signs everywhere.

questions.question: What does such a person feel about Allah’s nearness?
questions.answer: He feels his Lord is present and not far away.

questions.question: Why is it important not to treat created things as a wall?
questions.answer: Because they should help a person remember Allah, not hide Him.

questions.question: What words show the traveler was eager to continue learning?
questions.answer: He told himself to keep going.

questions.question: In the place he entered, how many great truths did he find?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: What lesson did the traveler learn from the people who often remember Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: He learned that tawhid is deep and has many stages.

questions.question: What kind of act is remembering Allah’s oneness called in the passage?
questions.answer: It is called a holy duty and an act of worship.

questions.question: Why did the traveler open a new “door” in his learning journey?
questions.answer: He wanted to move to a higher degree of understanding.

questions.question: Did he want pretend ideas or real understanding?
questions.answer: He wanted real understanding.

questions.question: What is one thing real understanding is based on?
questions.answer: It is based on proof.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does true tawhid include in the heart?
questions.answer: It includes believing, agreeing, and accepting.

questions.question: What can a person with this true belief do with all things around him?
questions.answer: He can find his Lord through them.

questions.question: How are the things in the world supposed to help a believer?
questions.answer: They are supposed to point him to Allah.

questions.question: If someone misses this truth, what hard thing might he think he has to do?
questions.answer: He might think he must remove the world to find Allah.

questions.question: What did the traveler say to his own self before moving on?
questions.answer: He told himself to go forward.

questions.question: What two ideas are named at the door he approached?
questions.answer: Allah’s greatness and majesty.

questions.question: What was spread through the whole cosmos in the new stopping-place?
questions.answer: Five wide truths proving Allah’s unity.

questions.question: What habit of believers made the traveler think more deeply?
questions.answer: Their constant saying of words about Allah being One.

questions.question: How does the passage describe this remembrance as an action?
questions.answer: It is worship and a blessed job of the soul.

questions.question: What was the traveler hoping to gain by going farther?
questions.answer: A higher and truer level of knowing Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What kind of knowledge is not enough in this passage?
questions.answer: A knowledge that is only in the imagination.

questions.question: What kind of knowledge is better than that?
questions.answer: Knowledge that is firm and comes from evidence.

questions.question: What does true tawhid help a person realize about Allah and the world?
questions.answer: Allah can be known through everything in the world.

questions.question: How should all things appear to someone with strong faith?
questions.answer: Like paths that lead to the Creator.

questions.question: What wrong idea does the passage warn against?
questions.answer: Thinking creation keeps a person away from Allah.

questions.question: Why would that wrong idea make faith harder?
questions.answer: Because then a person would think he must clear away everything first.

questions.question: Where did the traveler enter after calling himself onward?
questions.answer: He entered a place about Allah’s actions and making things.

questions.question: What did he witness there that supported tawhid?
questions.answer: Five clear truths over the whole universe.

questions.question: What words were repeated by people of faith in the passage?
questions.answer: Words that say only Allah is truly God.

questions.question: What did the traveler understand from their repeating those words?
questions.answer: He understood that tawhid has many levels to learn.

questions.question: Name one way the passage describes this remembrance.
questions.answer: It is joyful.

questions.question: Name another way it describes it.
questions.answer: It is valuable and worship.

questions.question: Why did the traveler want another stopping-place?
questions.answer: He wanted to grow more in understanding.

questions.question: What does the passage say true tawhid is more than?
questions.answer: It is more than a thought in the mind.

questions.question: What does true tawhid need in order to be strong?
questions.answer: It needs proof and true acceptance.

questions.question: What does the heart do in true tawhid?
questions.answer: It confirms and accepts Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: When looking at all things, what should a believer find?
questions.answer: A way leading to the Creator.

questions.question: What should a believer not call the things in the world?
questions.answer: He should not call them a barrier to Allah.

questions.question: What final discovery did the traveler make in that place?
questions.answer: He saw five broad truths that clearly proved Allah is One.

questions.question: Who are the two groups mentioned as often repeating words of Allah’s oneness?
questions.answer: Believers in general and especially people in a Sufi order.

questions.question: What did their practice point to?
questions.answer: It pointed to many degrees in affirming Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What was the traveler searching for beyond simple repeating?
questions.answer: He was searching for deeper, true understanding.

questions.question: What kind of understanding was rejected?
questions.answer: An understanding that is only imagined.

questions.question: What kind of understanding was accepted?
questions.answer: One that comes from proof and sure knowledge.

questions.question: What four heart actions are part of true tawhid in the passage?
questions.answer: Judging, confirming, agreeing, and accepting.

questions.question: What does this true tawhid let a person sense about his Lord?
questions.answer: That his Lord is present with all things.

questions.question: How does a person with this faith view creation?
questions.answer: As signs that guide him to Allah.

questions.question: What mistake would make a person feel far from Allah?
questions.answer: Thinking the world stands in the way.

questions.question: After deciding to continue, what doorway did the traveler approach?
questions.answer: The doorway of Allah’s greatness and majesty.

questions.question: What did he find in the world of creation?
questions.answer: Five great truths ruling over the universe and proving Divine unity.
